# Results — Study 118 (Fed-Model) on the Shiller monthly dataset

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Data source: Shiller S&P 500
monthly dataset, staged at `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`. Earnings yield
(E/P = Earnings/SP500); 10y nominal yield = Long Interest Rate / 100; real rate = nominal
yield minus trailing 12m CPI inflation. Forward real total returns compound monthly real
total return (Real Price pct-change + Real Dividend / Real Price / 12). As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 (EP, rate, real returns) | 1871-01 to 2023-06 | `00642a8c9b41` |

Valid rows (Earnings > 0, rate > 0, SP500 > 0): **1,830**. Forward 10yr returns available
through 2013-06 (n = 1,710); forward 1yr returns through 2022-06 (n = 1,818).

## In-sample OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors

Overlapping 10-year returns are correlated across ~119 consecutive months. We apply 120 HAC
lags (matching the overlap window) to avoid inflating the t-statistic.

| Signal | Horizon | Slope | R² | HAC t (120 lags) | n |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fed-Model spread** (E/P − 10y nominal) | 10yr | **+0.535** | **0.117** | **+1.78** | 1,710 |
| Fed-Model spread | 1yr | +0.746 | 0.015 | +1.74 | 1,818 |
| **Earnings yield (E/P)** | 10yr | **+0.933** | **0.242** | **+4.98** | 1,710 |
| E/P vs real rate (Asness) | 10yr | +0.212 | 0.087 | +2.63 | 1,698 |
| E/P vs real rate (Asness) | 1yr | −0.221 | 0.006 | −1.13 | 1,806 |

Key readings:
- **The Fed-Model spread at 10yr**: HAC *t* = **+1.78** — *below* the |t| ≥ 2 bar with proper
  overlap correction (naive OLS t without overlap correction would be ~15, badly misleading).
- **E/P alone is stronger**: HAC t = +4.98 and R² = 0.242 — earnings yield beats the composite
  spread because adding the nominal rate (a mostly-irrelevant real/nominal confusion) dilutes
  the signal.
- **The Asness critique is confirmed**: E/P vs the real rate has HAC t = +2.63 at 10yr,
  but the 1yr coefficient is *negative* — the cross-real-rate spread is not a robust 1-year
  timing signal.

## Out-of-sample R² (Campbell & Thompson 2008)

Train on 1871–1969; predict 1970–2023. OOS R² < 0 means the unconditional historical mean
beats the regression model.

| Signal | Target | OOS R² | n_train | n_test |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fed-Model spread** | fwd10 | **−1.170** | 1,188 | 522 |
| Earnings yield (E/P) | fwd10 | **−0.003** | 1,188 | 522 |
| E/P vs real rate | fwd10 | +0.019 | 1,176 | 522 |
| Fed-Model spread | fwd1 | **−0.074** | 1,188 | 630 |

The Fed-Model spread's OOS R² is **−1.17**: the model's predictions are dramatically *worse*
than just guessing the historical mean. The reason is a structural regime shift: the model
is calibrated on a world where rates were low and rising E/P meant cheap stocks; in the
post-1970 era of high nominal rates the spread mechanically turns negative even when stocks
are reasonably valued, producing a systematic upward bias in predicted returns that never
materialized. E/P alone is marginally better (OOS R² ≈ −0.003, essentially zero).

## 1-year market-timing strategy (long when spread > expanding median)

| Arm | Mean return/yr | Sharpe | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Fed-Model timing (long when E/P > rate) | **+4.6%** | 1.15 | +5.91 |
| Buy & hold (unconditional) | **+8.6%** | 1.54 | — |
| **Active return** | **−4.0%/yr** | — | **−4.71** |

The timing strategy is *significantly worse* than buy-and-hold: active return −4.0%/yr,
HAC t = −4.71. The Fed-Model's "stocks are cheap" signal fires ~80% of the time (the spread
is almost always positive in the data), meaning the strategy is rarely long but misses a
large fraction of bull-market months.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** E/P alone has in-sample HAC t = +4.98 at 10yr, but OOS R² ≈ −0.003
  (the model barely beats the historical mean out of sample). The composite Fed-Model spread
  (E/P minus nominal yield) has HAC t = +1.78 — below the inference bar even in-sample — and
  catastrophic OOS R² of −1.17 due to interest-rate regime shifts. The 1-year signal is
  economically tiny (R² = 0.015) and structurally noisy. Literature support for E/P
  predictability is real but well-known and already widely arbitraged.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The 10-year signal requires a 10-year holding horizon
  (untradable in any conventional sense). The 1-year timing version *underperforms*
  buy-and-hold by −4%/yr (HAC t = −4.71). There is no implementable version of the Fed
  Model that outperforms passive indexing after accounting for the opportunity cost of
  sitting out of the market when the signal fires incorrectly.
- **Asness Critique Confirmed.** Comparing E/P to the nominal Treasury yield (the classic
  Fed Model) confuses real and nominal quantities. The real-rate version (E/P vs TIPS-proxy
  real rate) has a slightly better OOS R² (+0.019 vs −0.003 for E/P), but it remains a
  marginal improvement and the 1-year coefficient is *negative* — the critique is correct and
  the "fix" doesn't rescue the model as a timing tool.
